chunk_findings.detail: `_three_valued` does `(raw.get("verified") or {}).get("unverified")`. A malformed descriptor with a top-level scalar such as `verified = "yes"` (instead of a `[verified]` table) passes `_unknown_keys` without complaint, then `_three_valued` calls `.get()` on the string and raises `AttributeError`. `harness_lint` does not catch this, so `ddflow harness lint` crashes instead of reporting a lint problem for malformed input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness_drv.py:_three_valued

chunk_findings.detail: `skeleton` interpolates the free-form `family` and `title` arguments directly into TOML basic strings without escaping. For example, `harness_add(..., title='a"b')` writes `title = "a"b"`, which is invalid TOML, and a `family` containing `"`, `\`, or a newline is likewise invalid. The call still reports success, leaving the user with a descriptor that cannot be parsed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness_drv.py:skeleton

chunk_findings.detail: `model_show` applies `redact_network` only to the assembled `message`, but returns `facts=rows` with unredacted `source` and `v` values. `cmd_model` then passes every non-`message` key, including `facts`, to `Ctx.out`, so the CLI displays those raw values. Given a model row whose `src` resolves to `https://secret.example.com/models.toml` (or a fact value containing an endpoint address), the `message` line is redacted but the `facts` body is printed unchanged, defeating the promised network redaction.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/model_cmds.py:model_show (and ddflow/surfaces/commands/harness.py:cmd_model)

chunk_findings.detail: The action help says `harness_probe (reports what it would run, never runs it)`, but the change intent states probe writes a fact to the local layer. A user running `ddflow hooks --help` is told the command is side-effect free; when they run `ddflow hooks harness_probe --harness X`, the intended implementation will mutate local facts, contrary to the documented promise.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/hooks.py:Param("action")

chunk_findings.detail: The new command declarations add only `Command(path=("model",), ...)` and `Command(path=("model", "show"), ...)`. There are no declarations for `("model", "lint")`, `("model", "probe")`, or `("model", "resolve")`, and the manifest shows only `model_show` in api/model_cmds.py. Because the stated intent requires `ddflow model lint`, `ddflow model probe`, and `ddflow model resolve`, running `ddflow model resolve` after this change will not be registered and will fail as an unknown command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/hooks.py:Command(path=("model",...))

chunk_findings.detail: The test writes `[route.mine]` with endpoint `http://[REDACTED:ipv4]:8000/v1` but then calls `M.model_show(tmp_path, "mine-1")`. `mine-1` is a different `[model.mine-1]` record with no declared connection to the `mine` route, so the queried model never resolves the route endpoint being tested; if `M.model_show(tmp_path, "mine")` leaked that endpoint, this test would still pass. It also only checks `[REDACTED:ipv4]` in `out.data["message"]`, not in `str(out.data)`, even though the same test checks the model note endpoint in `str(out.data)`, leaving non-message route-endpoint leaks undetected.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_cli_drivers.py:test_model_show_never_prints_a_route_endpoint

chunk_findings.detail: `harness_lint` crashes on a syntactically valid TOML descriptor that sets `verified = true` (or any non-dict truthy value for `verified`). `_three_valued` does `raw.get("verified") or {}` and immediately calls `.get("unverified")`; if `verified` is `true`, this is `(True).get(...)`, raising `AttributeError`. `harness_lint` only catches `tomllib.TOMLDecodeError`, so the exception escapes instead of returning `O.failed` with a lint problem. A file containing `verified = true` (a plausible typo for `[verified]`) triggers the crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness_drv.py:_three_valued

chunk_findings.detail: `skeleton` inserts `family` and `title` directly into a TOML basic string without escaping. For example `title = 'My "harness"'` produces the line `title = "My "harness""`, which is invalid TOML. `harness_add` then writes an unparseable descriptor even though the title is legitimate input. `family` has the same issue. The function should TOML-escape these free-text strings or reject them explicitly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/harness_drv.py:skeleton

chunk_findings.detail: Only the human-readable `message` string is passed through `redact_network`; the `facts` list returned in `O.ok(... facts=rows ...)` still contains raw `v` values and raw source `url`/`path` strings. `cmd_model` then passes `facts` into the body given to `c.out`, so `ddflow model show <name>` can display unredacted endpoint addresses and source URLs despite the module docstring’s guarantee that “what is shown goes through the network redaction.” Example: a model fact with key `api` and `v = "http://[REDACTED:ipv4]:8080/token"` is not `endpoint`, so `_facts` includes it, the message line is redacted, but the fact body shown by `c.out` contains the raw URL.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/model_cmds.py:model_show, ddflow/surfaces/commands/harness.py:cmd_model

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text for `harness_probe` says it “reports what it would run, never runs it,” but the change intent states probe “writes a fact to the local layer.” A user running `ddflow harness probe --harness X` after reading `--help` will expect a dry run; if the implementation actually writes the fact, this is an unexpected side effect, and if it only reports, it fails the required behavior. Either way the shipped description is wrong for the specified command behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/hooks.py:action help

chunk_findings.detail: The diff wires only `model_show`: the call lambda has a branch only for `a.get("action") == "model_show"`, and the added covered paths are `("model",)` and `("model", "show")`. The stated intent includes `ddflow model lint`, `ddflow model probe`, and `ddflow model resolve`, but the manifest’s other files show no additions for those verbs (`ddflow/api/model_cmds.py` adds only `_source`, `_facts`, `model_show`). A user running `ddflow model lint` (or `probe`/`resolve`) will not get the intended command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/hooks.py:Command(path=("model",), ...) and call branch

chunk_findings.detail: The new parser registration helper is defined but never invoked. `register` is the only function in this file that receives the root subparsers, and the diff adds no call to `_harness_parsers(s)`, so none of the new `harness` subcommands (`add`, `lint`, `test`, `probe`, `facts`) or the new `model` command are installed. Reproduction: after applying the change, run `ddflow harness lint agent.toml` or `ddflow model show gpt-4o`; argparse will reject `lint`/`model` as unknown choices because the helper was not attached to the root parser. The imported `cmd_model` is likewise unused unless another file imports this private function.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/parsers/workflow.py:_harness_parsers

chunk_findings.detail: `test_probe_with_consent_runs_version_only` does not require `seen` to be non-empty. `all(a[1:] == ["--version"] for a in seen)` is vacuously `True` when `seen == []`. An implementation of `H.harness_view(..., what="probe", id="claude", run=True)` that returns any non-`O.NOTHING` outcome without ever invoking `D.EP.run` would still pass this test, so the test fails to catch a broken probe path it is meant to verify.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_harness_cli_drivers.py:92

chunk_findings.detail: The manifest for this change contains only implementation and test files and no ddflow self-assessment record. This violates [r-ddflow-self-assessment], which requires filing found ddflow bugs, misbehavior, or missing features at the end of every agent run/phase.
chunk_findings.title: r-ddflow-self-assessment
